variant: Cessna P210N Pressurized Centurion (1978-1983 model years, S/N P21000001-P21000834, 834 built). Geometry/perf from 1980-model POH and TCDS 3A21 Rev 47. NOTE: 1985-86 pressurized aircraft are the P210R (S/N 835-874, 40 built, TSIO-520-CE 325 hp, longer-span wing and stabilizer, 4100 lb) - not the P210N.
config: tractor, high cantilever wing, conventional tail

span.note: 36 ft 9 in, POH Fig 1-1 three-view (PDF p.11); Jane's 1982-83 via Wikipedia agrees

area.note: POH Fig 1-1 note 5 'Wing area is 175 square feet'; POH wing loading 22.9 lb/ft2 at 4000 lb. Implied AR 7.7.

root_chord.note: Wikipedia (uncited prose): constant 64 in chord from centerline to WS 100, straight taper to 44 in at WS 208. Consistent with POH: 2x(100x64+108x54)=170 ft2 to WS 208 plus tips ~ 175 ft2.

tip_chord.note: At WS 208 (34.7 ft station span); remaining ~12.5 in per side is tip fairing to reach 36.75 ft.

wing.airfoil: NACA 64A215 root / NACA 64A412 tip (Cessna 210, 1967-later cantilever wing) per Lednicer/Selig 'Incomplete Guide to Airfoil Usage' https://m-selig.ae.illinois.edu/ads/aircraft.html. Not confirmed against a Cessna drawing. Semi-Fowler flaps, 30 deg max (TCDS).
wing.winglets: no (Flint tip tanks, aftermarket, add ~33 gal and ~2 ft span per AvWeb)

vtail.note: Swept fin; overall aircraft height 9 ft 8 in max (POH). Fin dimensions not found.

cabin_width.note: 3 ft 8 in, GlobalAir spec page (secondary; not from Cessna doc)

fuselage.note: Overall height 9 ft 8 in max (POH). Pressurized 3.35 psi max differential (AOPA Pilot June 1978; AvWeb); four small windows per side; single left door; 200 lb baggage aft of rear pressure bulkhead. Pressurization from P337 system, based on T210M (NZ CAA TAR https://avsec.govt.nz/assets/aircraft/type-acceptance-reports/Cessna_210_Series.pdf).

gear: retractable tricycle, hydraulic, tubular-steel main legs; 1978 models had main gear doors, removed from 1979 (gear operating speed raised 140 to 165 KIAS; extended speed 200 KIAS) per TCDS 3A21 and AvWeb. Track 8 ft 8 in, wheelbase 72 in (POH Fig 1-1).
cooling: air-cooled, cowl flaps (improved for 1982 to reduce overcooling on descent); bleed air from turbo induction for pressurization; aftermarket intercoolers (Riley etc.) common; chronic hot-running engine at altitude (AvWeb)

diameter.note: McCauley D3A34C402/90DFA-10, diameter not over 80 in, not under 78.5 in (TCDS 3A21 Rev 47 sec XV). POH: 3-blade constant speed, 80 in. NOTE Wikipedia's 7 ft 6 in is wrong for the P210N.

rpm_cruise.note: typical POH cruise rows 2200-2600 rpm; max continuous 2600

engine.model: Continental TSIO-520-P (S/N P21000001-760); TSIO-520-AF (S/N 761 and up, 1982-83)

hp.note: Max continuous 285 hp at 2600 rpm; takeoff 310 hp at 2700 rpm, 5 min (TCDS 3A21; POH). -P: 36.5/33.5 in MP; -AF: 35.5/34.5 in MP.

mtow.note: takeoff and flight; ramp 4016 lb (S/N 151 and up)

empty.note: standard empty weight, 1980 model POH Performance-Specifications; Pressurized Centurion II (avionics pkg) 2406 lb. Jane's 1982-83 via Wikipedia: 2303 lb.

fuel_usable.note: 90 gal total, 89 usable S/N 1-760; 87 usable S/N 761+ (1982-83 fuel system with L/R/BOTH selector and vapor return). Owners report difficulty actually loading full 89 gal (AvWeb).

ntsb_total.note: NTSB CAROL API query 2026-10-24, Aircraft.AircraftModel contains 'P210' or 'P-210' (strings P210, P210N, P210R, P210N II, P210 - N, P-210N, P-210, plus one Robertson P210N; one mis-tagged '180' dropped): 296 records = 291 accidents + 5 incidents, 1978-10-14 to 2026-10-04, worldwide incl. 19 foreign/NTSB-assisted. P210N-labelled only: 223 accidents. P210R: 10. US only: 277 records. Includes turbine (Silver Eagle) conversions registered as P210N. Aircraft logged as plain '210N' cannot be separated.

ntsb_fatal.note: 78 fatal events, 162 deaths (cm_fatalInjuryCount summed over case records); US only 68 fatal events / 139 deaths. P210N-labelled 59 fatal accidents; P210R 4. Whole Cessna 210 family (model contains '210', make Cessna, excluding 205/210-5): 3,376 accidents, 718 fatal (US 3,209 / 622) - CAROL pre-1982 coverage may be incomplete and API flagged MaxResultCountReached, so treat as a floor.

fleet_size_for_rate.note: P210N S/N P21000001-834 (TCDS); plus 40 P210R. Fatal-event share 78/874 airframes ~ 9% over 48 years (my arithmetic, no exposure hours).

safety.pattern: RECORD (NTSB text, keyword screen of ProbableCause/analysis narrative for 296 cases, 243 with text): any engine power loss mentioned in 81 cases (13 fatal); fuel exhaustion/starvation/mismanagement 39 (6 fatal); landing-gear (gear-up, collapse, failure to extend) 53 (2 fatal); fire 7 (4 fatal); icing 11 (9 fatal); vacuum/gyro failure 5 (5 fatal). My hand-read of the 78 fatal causes: roughly 36 weather/IMC/night/icing/turbulence related (6 in-flight breakups from overstress, 4 following vacuum/gyro failure), ~11 piston engine mechanical failures dominated by oil-system/maintenance faults (oil lines, turbo oil line, oil pump bushings, con-rod oil passage, crankcase torque, one P210R detonation piston failure), 2 mixture mismanagement, 5 fuel exhaustion/starvation, 2 in-flight engine-compartment fires (oil leak; turbo wastegate), remainder stall/takeoff/incapacitation/impairment. HISTORY: 1980 pair of fatal crashes from detonation -> emergency ADs for rich mixture, 1981 Cessna-paid turbo retrofit AD; 50-hour exhaust-crack AD for non-Inconel exhausts; 1982 fuel system change (L/R/BOTH selector) to cut mismanagement (AvWeb https://avweb.com/features/cessna-p210-centurion/). 210-family cantilever carry-through spar fatigue/corrosion ADs (2012 emergency AD; AD 2020-03-16 after 2019 T210M wing separation, ATSB AO-2019-026). INFERENCE: configuration-linked risks are the hot-running bleed-pressurized TSIO-520 (detonation, cooling, exhaust cracks), complex gear (high count of gear-up/collapse, mostly non-fatal), and single vacuum system in IMC on older units; fatal record is dominated by pilot/weather like other high-performance IFR singles.

why_died_detail: Not a failed design: 834 P210N + 40 P210R built. Production ended with Cessna's 1986 shutdown of piston singles (product-liability era). Weaknesses: bleed-air pressurization from a TSIO-520 that ran hot; detonation crashes 1980 forced rich-mixture ADs and a 1981 turbo retrofit that cut altitude performance ('sick dog at altitude' - owner, AvWeb); only 3.35 psi (~10,000 ft cabin at FL200) vs Malibu 5.5 psi; realistic ceiling FL190; short range on 89 gal; single door. P210R (1985) fixed much of this (325 hp, longer wing, 115 gal option) but came too late. Aftermarket fixes: Vitatoe TN550 turbonormalized IO-550, Silver Eagle Allison 250 turboprop (114 conversions by 2023). Directly relevant to the revival question: the airframe works; engine/pressurization integration was the weak link.
rights_hints: Type Certificate 3A21 held by Cessna Aircraft Co., now Textron Aviation (Wichita); TCDS 3A21 Rev 49 dated 29 July 2015 cited by NZ CAA TAR rev 5 (https://avsec.govt.nz/assets/aircraft/type-acceptance-reports/Cessna_210_Series.pdf), which notes the TC holder 'provided access to all technical publications'. STC holders: Griggs Aircraft Refinishing (Silver Eagle turboprop, formerly O&N), Vitatoe Aviation (TN550), Flint Aero (tip tanks), Riley (intercooler/Super P210).
